h.strategy: Propose hypotheses where the condition plausibly changes the edit's effect by a large amount through a simple mechanism: redundancy (an alternative path or component already provides what the edit adds), disconnection (the edited part cannot influence the outcome under the condition), saturation (gains shrink when capacity is already high), or bottleneck (gains grow when the edited part is the limiting factor). Make sure the direction follows unambiguously from the mechanism. Avoid conditions unrelated to the edited part.

hyps.why: Upgrading a dead direct edge to a conv restores a path to the output and gains more than upgrading an already-alive skip or pool.
Edge 5 is the last hop from node 2, so replacing none restores that route and gains more than upgrading an existing op.
With edge 1 removed, edge 2 is the only way into node 2, so its capacity is the limiting factor.
A direct skip into node 3 already supplies a residual path, so the extra conv on edge 4 is partly redundant.
With edge 2 removed, node 2 is fed only by edge 1, so edge 5 sees less signal and the conv gains less.
Restoring a direct skip from none is a large gain, whereas replacing a conv or pool with skip loses accuracy.
A parallel direct skip cushions the degradation from pooling on edge 4, so the effect is less negative.
The direct skip keeps input reaching the output, so cutting edge 0 costs less.
The bypass cushions the loss of the deep route through edge 5, so removal hurts less.
With a direct skip into node 3 already present, edge 4 is more redundant and removing it costs less.
